data.hypothesis: Precomputing the y- and z-neighbor line pointers once per row should reduce repeated address-offset work in the inner x loop while retaining contiguous accesses for compiler vectorization. A guarded, unhinted OpenMP SIMD directive is supported by earlier valid candidates in this build; starting all pointers at x0 avoids any false alignment claim. Whether this distinct pointer-hoisted formulation improves on the existing SIMD candidates remains to be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this unfused stencil kernel, retain an unaligned SIMD path and measure alternative row-address formulations rather than assuming aligned allocations imply aligned interior starts.
memory_lessons.claim: Prior valid SIMD candidates measured between 0.0793 and 0.0844 seconds for several formulations, while the recorded simdlen(4) candidate measured 0.1436 seconds. These results do not establish a stable advantage for a particular alignment or width hint.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this row-pointer-hoisted formulation under the official settings against the best correctly validated candidate.

data.notes: This is a source proposal, not a measured result. Prior role measurements are useful comparisons but do not confirm a speedup for this candidate. The interior offset is included in each line base; no alignment assumption, compiler-flag change, threading, or spatial/temporal blocking is introduced.
transformations: Keep the single-timestep sweep, arithmetic grouping, bounds, buffer parity, and interface unchanged.
Precompute pointers for each y- and z-neighbor line once per x row, then traverse the contiguous interior x range with a zero-based index.
Guard an unhinted OpenMP SIMD directive for OpenMP 4.0 or later; leave the same loop available for compiler vectorization without the directive.
Base every line at x0 and make no alignment assertion, ISA assumption, compiler-flag change, threading change, or spatial/temporal blocking change.
